cards.front: Complete the rule: Consult the vehicle owner’s.
cards.back: Consult the vehicle owner’s manual for its starting procedure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In the park-and-drive starting sequence described, begin with.
cards.back: In the park-and-drive starting sequence described, begin with the selector in park and apply the brake.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Switch the ignition on to check warning.
cards.back: Switch the ignition on to check warning lights and gauges before engaging the engine.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After starting in the described sequence, switch.
cards.back: After starting in the described sequence, switch on low-beam headlights and lock the doors.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before moving forward in drive, check ahead, to.
cards.back: Before moving forward in drive, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal, then accelerate gradually.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Operate the accelerator with the front of the.
cards.back: Operate the accelerator with the front of the foot while keeping the heel on the floor.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The clutch friction point is where the engine.
cards.back: The clutch friction point is where the engine and transmission begin engaging as the pedal is released.

cards.front: Complete the rule: As you release a manual clutch, match the.
cards.back: As you release a manual clutch, match the vehicle’s forward or reverse movement with accelerator pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: To start moving a manual vehicle, hold the brake.
cards.back: To start moving a manual vehicle, hold the brake with the right foot and press the clutch fully down with the left.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Select first gear and release the parking.
cards.back: Select first gear and release the parking brake before moving off in the manual-start sequence.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal the intended direction, check mirrors and look.
cards.back: Signal the intended direction, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic before moving off.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Ease the clutch to the friction point while looking.
cards.back: Ease the clutch to the friction point while looking toward the road rather than at your hands or feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Move the right foot from brake to accelerator.
cards.back: Move the right foot from brake to accelerator, add gentle acceleration and finish releasing the clutch slowly.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A forward jerk during a manual start can mean.
cards.back: A forward jerk during a manual start can mean the clutch was released abruptly or too much accelerator was applied.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the vehicle lurches and stalls during the described.
cards.back: If the vehicle lurches and stalls during the described manual start, insufficient accelerator input is the stated cause.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Choose gears according to the driving task’s required.
cards.back: Choose gears according to the driving task’s required power and speed; first gear supplies starting power.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The manual gives fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour.
cards.back: The manual gives fifteen to twenty-five miles per hour as a second-gear example, depending on engine power and whether the transmission has three, four or five speeds.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Second gear can also be used to.
cards.back: Second gear can also be used to start on ice or drive through heavy snow.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a three-speed transmission, the manual generally describes.
cards.back: For a three-speed transmission, the manual generally describes third gear for speeds above twenty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a small-engine vehicle with a four- or five-speed.
cards.back: For a small-engine vehicle with a four- or five-speed transmission, the third-gear example extends to thirty or forty miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The manual describes fourth gear for driving above.
cards.back: The manual describes fourth gear for driving above thirty-five miles per hour on a flat road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Uphill driving may require reaching forty miles per.
cards.back: Uphill driving may require reaching forty miles per hour or more before selecting fourth or fifth gear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before an upshift, accelerate to a speed suitable for.
cards.back: Before an upshift, accelerate to a speed suitable for the intended gear, press the clutch fully down and release the accelerator.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Complete an upshift by selecting the next higher.
cards.back: Complete an upshift by selecting the next higher gear, applying accelerator input and progressively releasing the clutch.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Downshifting can provide more power, assist acceleration or.
cards.back: Downshifting can provide more power, assist acceleration or steering, and help slow or stop the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Downshifting to slow a descent is.
cards.back: Downshifting to slow a descent is advised except when the road is slippery.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a downshift, release the accelerator and use.
cards.back: For a downshift, release the accelerator and use the brake as well if you want to slow.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Press the clutch fully down and select a lower.
cards.back: Press the clutch fully down and select a lower gear; abrupt deceleration may require skipping to an even lower gear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After selecting a lower gear, release the clutch toward.
cards.back: After selecting a lower gear, release the clutch toward its friction point while adding accelerator pressure as needed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: To hold a manual vehicle for an uphill start.
cards.back: To hold a manual vehicle for an uphill start, set the parking brake, depress the clutch and choose first gear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For an uphill start, ease the clutch to engagement.
cards.back: For an uphill start, ease the clutch to engagement with gentle acceleration and release the parking brake when the vehicle begins pulling forward.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Continue accelerating in first gear during the uphill start.
cards.back: Continue accelerating in first gear during the uphill start until there is enough speed to shift to second.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before stopping, check rear traffic in the mirrors.
cards.back: Before stopping, check rear traffic in the mirrors, move to the brake and apply smooth, steady pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When stopping a manual vehicle, depress the.
cards.back: When stopping a manual vehicle, depress the clutch as the vehicle comes to a halt.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For an unexpected slowdown or stop, quickly tap the.
cards.back: For an unexpected slowdown or stop, quickly tap the brake pedal three or four times to alert the driver behind.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn the steering wheel toward the intended.
cards.back: Turn the steering wheel toward the intended direction in forward travel and in reverse.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use the nine-and-three or eight-and-four hand positions.
cards.back: Use the nine-and-three or eight-and-four hand positions for steering control and reduced airbag-injury risk.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Hold the wheel firmly but gently with the fingers.
cards.back: Hold the wheel firmly but gently with the fingers, keeping the thumbs along its face and avoiding a grip on the inside rim.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check behind the vehicle before entering because small objects.
cards.back: Check behind the vehicle before entering because small objects and children can be hidden from the driver’s seat.

cards.front: Complete the rule: To begin backing, start the vehicle.
cards.back: To begin backing, start the vehicle, apply the brake and select reverse.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For backing, place the left hand at twelve o’clock.
cards.back: For backing, place the left hand at twelve o’clock, rest the right arm behind the passenger seat and look through the rear window.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup.
cards.back: Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera when reversing; each leaves part of the rear area unseen.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Back no faster than a slow walking pace and.
cards.back: Back no faster than a slow walking pace and steer toward the intended movement of the vehicle’s rear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When turning in reverse, make brief checks ahead and.
cards.back: When turning in reverse, make brief checks ahead and to the sides while continuing to look rearward until fully stopped.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Minimize backing and.
cards.back: Minimize backing and avoid reversing into traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Back into a driveway or parking space unless.
cards.back: Back into a driveway or parking space unless signs prohibit it so you can leave facing forward.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook advises limiting idling around.
cards.back: The handbook advises limiting idling around a start or stop to one minute.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Gentle driving during the first few minutes.
cards.back: Gentle driving during the first few minutes warms the engine more efficiently than extended idling.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Idling wastes fuel.
cards.back: Idling wastes fuel and releases harmful pollutants.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Some Maine local governments.
cards.back: Some Maine local governments have ordinances restricting idling.
